title: Success And Limitations With Moderate Approach
definition: The Moderate phase (1885-1905) refers to the early period of the Indian National Congress characterized by 'Constitutional Agitation'—a policy of petitioning, prayer, and protest to secure gradual administrative and economic reforms within the British framework.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the evolution of Indian nationalism, the transition from 'mendicancy' to 'militancy', and the ideological foundations of the freedom struggle.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Success And Limitations With Moderate Approach.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
